Licence texts of the Rust crates in the WebAssembly of opaque.js

opaque.js is @serenity-kit/opaque 1.1.0 as npm published it (README.md
beside this file), under the package's own licence, opaque.LICENSE. Its
WebAssembly holds Rust crates under their own licences: this file holds
their texts. The package publishes no lock file, and its build's lock
is not published, so the crates and versions below are a
reconstruction, not the build's lock:

- the crates the WebAssembly names in the paths of their sources
  (<crate>-<version>/src/), at the versions named there: those of the
  package's dependency graph, and dlmalloc and hashbrown, which come
  with Rust's standard library;
- every other crate at the newest version of its series (the versions
  Cargo's caret requirement takes) on crates.io when npm published the
  package, 2026-02-01 14:40:35 UTC; resolved from the package's
  Cargo.toml at the commit npm's provenance names,
  ca1cb22f03b9e456159ce367e2975124f87f5ad8 of serenity-kit/opaque,
  with Cargo's resolver 1 (edition 2018, no resolver key), for
  wasm32-unknown-unknown, without dev dependencies, build dependencies,
  procedural macros and what only those use.

Of the crates of the package's dependency graph the WebAssembly names,
all but one are themselves the newest of their series at that time,
and the manifest pins the other, generic-array, at its version: so the
rule gives the WebAssembly's own versions back. No crate below was
published after that time, and none is yanked.

Rust's own core, alloc and std are in the WebAssembly too, built at
the Rust compiler's commit 254b59607d4417e9dffbc307138ae5c86280fe4c.
Their texts are not here: they are in Rust's repository at that
commit, under MIT or Apache-2.0. Which crates they use there was not
looked up (the lock file of Rust's library at that commit names
them); the WebAssembly names none of them but dlmalloc and hashbrown.

gives the files at its root named LICENSE*, LICENCE*, COPYING*, NOTICE*
or UNLICENSE*, and the one its Cargo.toml names as license-file, with

that is byte for byte one above is not written again: its line names
